note: Markdown provides a text-format filter (plugin id 'markdown'), a 'markdown' service (Drupal\markdown\Markdown) with parse()/getParser()/load()/loadFile()/loadUrl()/save(), a Twig |markdown filter and markdown() function, and three plugin types (parser, extension, allowed_html) with managers plugin.manager.markdown.parser/.extension/.allowed_html. Parser plugin ids on this site include commonmark, commonmark-gfm, parsedown, parsedown-extra, php-markdown, php-markdown-extra. Admin UI at markdown.overview (/admin/config/content/markdown, perm 'administer markdown'). A text format stores the filter at filters.markdown with status and settings.id (the parser). Cases are grounded in that real filter config: introspection reads back the configured parser on a live text format; execution enables the Markdown filter on a format and switches its parser, verified against the live filter_format config.

evals.prompt: On a Drupal 11 site with the Markdown module, how do I let editors write content in Markdown that renders to HTML? What do I add to a text format?
evals.expected_output: Enable the 'Markdown' filter (filter plugin id 'markdown') on a text format (Configuration > Content authoring > Text formats and editors). On the filter_format it is stored at filters.markdown.status = true with settings.id set to the chosen parser.

evals.prompt: With the Markdown module, how do I convert a Markdown string to HTML in custom PHP code, and how do I render Markdown from a Twig template?
evals.expected_output: Use the 'markdown' service: \Drupal::service('markdown')->parse($string) returns a ParsedMarkdown that stringifies to HTML (also loadFile()/loadUrl() for files/URLs). In Twig use the {{ var|markdown }} filter or markdown(var) function.

evals.prompt: Which Markdown parser libraries does the Drupal Markdown module support, and how are they made available? Name at least one parser plugin id.
evals.expected_output: It supports pluggable parsers backed by external Composer libraries: CommonMark (commonmark, commonmark-gfm), Parsedown (parsedown, parsedown-extra) and PHP Markdown (php-markdown, php-markdown-extra). You install the library via Composer (e.g. league/commonmark); the module detects installed parsers and marks missing ones. They are markdown.parser plugins.

evals.prompt: This Drupal site has a text format 'md_probe' that renders Markdown. Inspect its live configuration and state which Markdown parser plugin id its Markdown filter is configured to use.
evals.expected_output: The Markdown filter on md_probe uses the parsedown parser (filter.format.md_probe -> filters.markdown.settings.id = parsedown).

evals.prompt: Inspect the 'md_enabled' text format on this Drupal site and state which Markdown parser its Markdown filter uses.
evals.expected_output: The md_enabled format's Markdown filter uses the commonmark parser (filter.format.md_enabled -> filters.markdown.settings.id = commonmark).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, create a text format with machine id md_task named 'MD Task' that has the Markdown module's Markdown filter enabled, so content in that format is rendered from Markdown to HTML. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: A filter.format.md_task config entity exists with filters.markdown.status = true (the Markdown filter enabled, with a parser in settings.id).

evals.prompt: The text format 'md_switch' on this site uses the Markdown module with the CommonMark parser. Reconfigure its Markdown filter to use the Parsedown parser (parser id parsedown) instead, keeping the filter enabled. Apply the change live.
evals.expected_output: In filter.format.md_switch the Markdown filter stays enabled and filters.markdown.settings.id becomes 'parsedown'.
